# End-of-Year Dinner and March Launch: brief

## Assumptions

- Live end-of-year team dinner, without slides or Q&A.
- The speaker leads or represents the team.
- The audience already knows the product and the March launch context.
- The tone should be warm, sincere, and lightly energizing rather than corporate or comedic.
- No achievements or personal stories were supplied, so the speech makes no specific claims about results.
- The two-minute slot is a ceiling. Timing uses 130 words per minute and a 108-second limit, leaving room for natural delivery.

## Goal and message

**Goal — unconfirmed:** After this, the team will celebrate one another tonight and, on returning to work, bring focus and mutual support to the March launch.

**Selected message — unconfirmed:** This team made this year count—and March is ours.

The strongest message was selected without pausing for confirmation, as requested.

| Candidate | Retell | Headline | Banner | Three seconds |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| This team made this year count—and March is ours. | Pass | Pass | Pass | Pass |
| Tonight we celebrate the team; next, we make March count. | Pass | Pass | Pass | Pass |
| One team, one launch, one March to be proud of. | Pass | Pass | Pass | Pass |

## Arguments

| Tag | Listener value | Proof used in the speech |
|---|---|---|
| Your work | Each person feels seen and appreciated. | Visible and less-visible contributions are named in concrete, familiar terms without claiming specific results. |
| March launch | The coming launch gives the team a shared and exciting destination. | The user supplied the March launch; the speech connects it to the experience being created for the people the product serves. |
| This team | Everyone has agency without being asked for heroics. | The speech names practical actions within each person’s control: clear questions, careful choices, and strong handoffs. |

## Elephant in the room

At a dinner, people may resist having next year’s work turned into another corporate pep talk. The speech parks this by leading with genuine recognition, rejecting heroics, keeping the work message brief, and explicitly inviting everyone to enjoy tonight before returning to the launch.

## Structure

**Chosen structure:** Story/change blended with an occasion toast.

- **0:00–0:19 — Look around:** Recognize the people in the room and state the message.
- **0:19–0:36 — Your work:** Thank them for visible and less-visible contributions.
- **0:36–0:57 — March launch:** Turn the date into a shared destination.
- **0:57–1:20 — This team:** Replace heroics with clear, mutual action and summarize the three ideas.
- **1:20–1:40 — Toast and action:** Raise a glass, enjoy tonight, then return ready for the next decision and handoff.

No slides are needed.

# End-of-Year Dinner and March Launch: script

200 words = 92.3 s · 3 long pauses = 7.5 s · **total 99.8 s** · limit 108 s (90% of 2:00)

Cues: `/` short pause · `//` long pause · **bold** = stress

## Opening options

### Recommended — Connect

35 opening words · full speech 99.8 s

[MEMORIZE] Tonight, before we look ahead, look around. / Everyone here has put something of themselves into this team. / That deserves more than a quick “well done.” // This team made this year count—and March is ours.

### Alternative — Engage

34 opening words · full speech 99.3 s

[MEMORIZE] For a moment, forget the launch date. / Look at the people around you. / This is where March begins: with a team whose work matters. // This team made this year count—and March is ours.

### Alternative — Surprise

33 opening words · full speech 98.9 s

[MEMORIZE] March will not be made in one dramatic moment. / It will be made in the questions, choices, and handoffs that come before it. // This team made this year count—and March is ours.

---

## Main script

### Opening (0:00–0:19)

[MEMORIZE] Tonight, before we look ahead, look around. / Everyone here has put something of themselves into this team. / That deserves more than a quick “well done.” // This team made this year count—and March is ours.

### Your work (0:19–0:36)

First, thank you—for the work people saw, and the work they didn’t. /

[SKIP IF LATE] For your judgment, your care, and the ways you helped us move forward. /

Whatever your role, what you brought mattered. //

### March launch (0:36–0:57)

Our product launches in March. / A launch is more than a date. / It’s the moment many separate decisions become one clear experience for the people we’re building it for. /

We get to turn our work into something real, together. / That’s what makes March exciting.

### This team (0:57–1:20)

We don’t need one person to be a hero. / We need each person at their best: asking the clear question, making the careful choice, helping the next person succeed. /

One strong handoff at a time, March gets closer. /

So tonight, celebrate the work, trust the team, and look forward to March.

### Closing (1:20–1:40)

[MEMORIZE] Raise your glass: to your work, our March launch, and this team. // Enjoy tonight. / When we’re back, bring your best to the next decision and handoff. / This team made this year count. / **Now let’s make March ours.**

## Optional personal insert

Replace the final two sentences of “Your work” with a true version of this line, capped at 21 words:

> When [three-word moment], I saw what this team is made of: [quality]. That moment captured the care behind our work.

At 21 words, the personalized version runs about 100.3 seconds.

# End-of-Year Dinner and March Launch: cue cards

## Card 1: Opening [0:00]

“Tonight, before we look ahead, look around. /
Everyone here has put something of themselves into this team. /
That deserves more than a quick ‘well done.’ //
This team made this year count—and March is ours.”

## Card 2: Your work [0:19]

- visible + unseen work
- judgment · care · forward *(skip if late)*
- every role mattered
- pause
→ “Our product launches in March.”

## Card 3: March launch [0:36]

- more than a calendar date
- separate decisions → one experience
- work becomes real, together
- excitement
→ “We don’t need one person to be a hero.”

## Card 4: This team [0:57]

- no lone hero
- ask clearly · choose carefully · help next
- one strong handoff
- work · team · March
→ “Raise your glass.”

## Card 5: Closing [1:20]

“Raise your glass: to your work, our March launch, and this team. //
Enjoy tonight. /
When we’re back, bring your best to the next decision and handoff. /
This team made this year count. /
Now let’s make March ours.”

# End-of-Year Dinner and March Launch: rehearsal kit

## Timing

| Section | Starts | Lasts | Words | Long pauses | Skip if late? |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Opening | 0:00 | 18.7 s | 35 | 1 | No |
| Your work | 0:19 | 17.7 s | 33 | 1 | Judgment-and-care sentence only |
| March launch | 0:36 | 20.3 s | 44 | 0 | No |
| This team and summary | 0:57 | 23.5 s | 51 | 0 | No |
| Closing | 1:20 | 19.6 s | 37 | 1 | Never |
| **Total** |  | **99.8 s** | **200** | **3** | 8.2 s inside the 108 s limit |

## Practice plan

1. Read the speech aloud once. Simplify any line that catches in your mouth.
2. Deliver the opening and closing three times from memory. These carry the emotional weight.
3. Record one full run, aiming for 1:35–1:45. Check that each long pause is silent rather than filled with “um.”
4. Do one final run from the cue cards. Look up for each complete thought, especially during the toast.

## Three techniques

1. **Lighthouse eye contact:** On “look around,” actually look around. During the body, give one full thought to one person or table before moving your gaze.
2. **Pause and contrast:** Let the silence after “well done” and “mattered” do the emotional work. Add energy when the speech turns toward March.
3. **Grounded stillness:** Stand with both feet planted and keep the glass low. Raise it only after saying “Raise your glass,” making the closing feel deliberate.

## Day-of checklist

- Confirm where the speech falls in the dinner and whether a microphone is needed.
- Keep water nearby; save the first alcoholic drink until after speaking.
- Silence the phone and remove anything noisy from pockets.
- Run the first and final lines once.
- Wait until glasses are filled before beginning.
- Keep the closing even if an earlier speaker runs long; use the marked cut instead.

## Q&A

No Q&A is expected or needed for this occasion speech.
